title: Data governance bundles: pricing experiment for retention + compliance + premium SLA
creator: Claire Zhang
description: Run a matrixed pricing and contract experiment that bundles observability retention tiers, a Compliance Pack (security questionnaire + controls), and an optional Premium SLA offering. Objective is to validate willingness-to-pay, sales friction, and contract/legal implications for tiered add-ons focused on enterprise customers who require longer retention and explicit compliance controls.
hypothesis: Packaging longer observability retention (90/180 days), a standardized Compliance Pack, and an explicit Premium SLA as combinable addons will increase ASP and conversion in enterprise trials by >=15% without increasing sales cycle by more than 20%. We expect high-touch customers to prefer pre-bundled offers (Retention+Compliance+SLA) while mid-market will pick single add-ons.
acceptance_criteria: Define 3 canonical bundles and price points: Essentials (30d retention), Governance (90d + Compliance Pack), Enterprise (180d + Compliance Pack + Premium SLA)
Instrument pricing pages and conversation playbook for sales to offer bundles and single add-ons
Run A/B experiment for self-serve vs sales-assisted flows for 8 weeks
Collect baseline and experiment metrics: conversion, ASP, sales cycle length, legal review time
Legal and security sign-off on compliance pack scoping and contract clause templates
metrics: Average selling price (ASP) delta vs baseline
Sales cycle length (days) change for deals using bundles
Number of security questionnaire escalations per deal
Churn at 6 months for customers who purchased retention vs those who did not
experiments_plan: We will implement a 3x2 matrix: three bundle options (Essentials, Governance, Enterprise) crossed with channel (self-serve pricing page vs sales-assisted quote). Track cohort performance for 8 weeks, then run a follow-up 4-week pricing cadence test on Enterprise bundle price +/-10% to find elasticity. Use feature flags and console gating so we can enable/disable offerings per tenant.
rollout_plan: Week 0-2: Finalize bundle definitions, draft contract clause language for Compliance Pack and SLA response times
Week 2-4: Implement UI changes to pricing page and Console addon toggles; integrate telemetry for purchase funnel
Week 4-6: Pilot with two enterprise accounts (customer-sponsored pilots) via sales-assisted flow
Week 6-12: Run A/B across self-serve and sales channels; collect metrics and legal escalations
Week 12-14: Analyze results, draft recommendation (ship, revise, or kill), and prepare playbook for scale
updates: 2025-02-18: Ticket created with initial hypothesis and proposed bundles.
2025-02-25: Aligned with Sales Engineering on pilot accounts; Nora shared list of 6 accounts that may opt-in for pilot.
2025-03-01: Legal provided initial feedback on SLA wording; requests clarity on liability cap and reporting cadence for incidents.
2025-03-04: Engineering scoped UI changes and estimated 2 sprints (Platform + Billing + Console). Security requested format for Compliance Pack evidence bundle.
review_feedback: Legal (2025-02-28): Prefer fixed-term addendum for retention over open-ended contract language; require explicit data deletion clause.
Security (2025-03-01): Compliance Pack should include SOC2 control mapping and a pre-built evidence export; escalate to Security ops for automation feasibility.
Sales (2025-03-03): Suggest a pilot discount on Enterprise bundle to reduce friction for early adopters; track net-new ARR and incremental spend separately.
notes: Avoid launching full audit support initially; scope Compliance Pack to questionnaire + controls mapping + sample evidence export. If pilot shows demand, build automation for evidence exports and longer-term contract term templates. Ensure Console displays active retention and compliance add-ons clearly per tenant.
